verdict.reason:
I couldn't refute the gap. Searching all of tests/ (unit, integration, e2e), the only test that checks a return's tax_summary is tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:232. It covers a sales return with one Add row and asserts [(-50, -9.5)]. The e2e return tests (tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:534 for the sales return, :596 for the debit note) check the sales summary with no Deduct row, and the debit note's tax_summary not at all. The Deduct tests, tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay.py:166 and test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:162-176, use plain invoices whose item amounts are positive.

So nothing reaches the branch at src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:212, `taxable = -abs(taxable) if detail.get("item_row") in negative`, with an item row in the `negative` set built at :203. Running mutmut show confirms the named mutants change exactly that code. 22, 25 and 30 empty or misread the negative set. 70 forces the condition False. 72 turns -abs into +abs. 74 and 76 misread item_row. On a debit note with the reverse-charge template, every one of these makes the Deduct row's taxable_amount positive while its tax_amount stays negative. That breaks REQ-001-PRS-F022 ("its `taxable_amount` the sign of its item rows' amounts, however ERPNext stored a Deduct row's details") and the DoD item "A return draft's entries are negative, as its tax rows' `tax_amount`".

The test can therefore be written within the current specs, with no spec or code change: a purchase return on the reverse-charge Add/Deduct template, with the Deduct details stored both ways, asserting negative taxable_amount and tax_amount on both entries.

Mutant 36 (`< 0` changed to `< 1`) differs only for item amounts between 0 and 1 and is close to equivalent. The other mutants are enough to justify the test.

claim: An `offset` of 10,001, a quantity with 4 decimal places and a `to_date` before `from_date` are checked to be refused naming the input, but no test checks that the refusal names the rule.
evidence: test_master_data.py::test_inputs_outside_the_schema_are_refused_before_erpnext ({"offset": 10001}, "offset"), test_return_drafts.py::test_inputs_outside_the_schema_are_refused (qty 1.0001, "items.0.qty: "), test_order_to_cash.py::test_invalid_invoice_filters_are_refused_before_erpnext and test_bank_and_cash.py::test_a_bank_transaction_list_breaking_a_rule_is_refused (from/to order, "from_date"). None asserts the rule text, such as shapes.in_order's "from_date must not be after to_date" or pydantic's limit and decimal-places messages. The unit test test_quantities_allow_3_decimal_places_and_no_more checks only that a ValidationError is raised.
proposal: Extend these cases to assert the rule as well: e.g. "offset: Input should be less than or equal to 10000", "items.0.qty: Decimal input should have no more than 3 decimal places", "from_date must not be after to_date" (exact strings as Enterich renders them).

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. The first Definition of Done item of REQ-001-PRS-F014 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:382) says the three inputs are refused "naming the input and the rule". No test checks the rule part for any of the three cases:
- `offset` of 10001: tests/integration/test_master_data.py:106 only checks that the text contains "offset".
- Quantity with 4 decimal places: tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:309 only checks for "items.0.qty: ". tests/unit/test_shapes.py:83-88 only checks that a ValidationError is raised, not its message.
- `to_date` before `from_date`: tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:232 and tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash.py:324 only check for "from_date". The rule text is raised at src/enterich/shapes.py:91 ("from_date must not be after to_date").

I searched all of tests/, including tests/e2e. No test contains "must not be after", "less than or equal" or "decimal places". In the e2e tests, `offset` and `qty` appear only with valid values.

The refusal text comes from src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:333-339 as "{loc}: {msg}". The rule is therefore observable, and it is required by the spec. Other tests already assert pydantic messages for other inputs, e.g. "accounts: List should have at least 2 items" at tests/integration/test_record_to_report_drafts.py:195. Because none of the three DoD cases does the same, a mutant that changes or removes in_order's message, or one of these limits' messages, would go unnoticed for these cases.

Closing the gap needs only stronger assertions in the existing parametrized cases (the exact strings as Enterich renders them). That is within the current specs, so the class is fix.

claim: The 403 and 404 half ("for 403 and 404 the text of REQ-001-PRS-F009" for a refusal without `_server_messages`) is untested. Every 403/404 the tests send comes from `error()`, which always adds `_server_messages` and an exc_type.
evidence: tests/fakes/erpnext.py error() always sets _server_messages, and _missing() uses it. test_unit test_a_refusal_without_messages_carries_status_and_type covers only a 417. test_master_data.py::test_an_unknown_or_unpermitted_name_names_the_input and test_order_to_cash_drafts.py::test_an_unknown_or_unpermitted_template_names_the_input both send full error bodies. A get_named that keyed on exc_type or on the message instead of the status would pass.
proposal: Add a parametrized test with erp.fail("/api/method/frappe.client.get", status, {}) and with {"exc_type": "PermissionError"}, for 403 and 404. Assert the tool error is the REQ-001-PRS-F009 text naming the input ("doesn't exist", "isn't permitted").

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. The third DoD item of REQ-001-PRS-F008 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:304) says a refusal without `_server_messages` gives the status and `exc_type`, or the REQ-001-PRS-F009 text for a 403 or 404. The code does this: get_named (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:202) looks only at `refused.status in (403, 404)`. Erpnext._refusal (src/enterich/erpnext.py:238) builds Refused with a None exc_type and no message when the body lacks them. No test sends such a 403 or 404:
- tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:164 only sends a 417 with `{"exc_type": "ValidationError"}`.
- tests/integration/test_master_data.py:243 and tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:281 send full `error()` bodies with a matching exc_type (DoesNotExistError, PermissionError) and a message.
- The fake's own 403 and 404 answers (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:389, :438, and :945 via _missing/_refused) also use full bodies.
- Every other `.fail(` call in tests/ that doesn't use `error()` has status 200 or 502.
- The e2e tests (tests/e2e/test_rights.py:99, tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:525) run against real ERPNext, which always sends `_server_messages`.

So a get_named that keyed on `exc_type in ("PermissionError", "DoesNotExistError")` instead of the status would pass every current test, while a bare 403 or 404 (body `{}`, `{"exc_type": ...}` only, or not JSON) would reach the agent as "ERPNext refused the request (404)." rather than the REQ-001-PRS-F009 text. The behaviour is required by the spec and can be seen in the tool error. A parametrized integration test (403 and 404, with bodies `{}` and `{"exc_type": "PermissionError"}`) through get_item, asserting "item_code", "doesn't exist" and "isn't permitted", closes the gap within the current specs. No code change is needed.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. `list_templates` (src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:254-269) sends fields=TEMPLATE_FIELDS, order_by "name asc", start=offset and page_length=limit+1, then returns page(records, offset, limit). The tests check less than that:

- tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:398 checks path, fields, filters and order_by, plus result["records"]. It never checks limit_start or limit_page_length, and never checks count, offset or has_more.
- test_disabled_templates_only_when_asked_for (test_order_to_cash.py:419) checks filters only.
- tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py:200 calls both tools with limit 50 and reads only names and is_default.
- tests/e2e/test_rights.py:238/244 only calls the tools, and test_tool_list.py:75 only checks description text.

No test anywhere in tests/ asserts paging for the template lists. The `has_more` and `limit_start` hits are all for other tools.

claim: The log-level item is tested only by calling log.configure('ERROR') directly. No test sets ENTERICH_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR and starts Enterich, so the path from the variable through main() to the log configuration is unchecked.
evidence: tests/unit/test_log.py::test_the_level_filters_library_lines_only calls log.configure('ERROR', stream). tests/unit/test_main.py never sets ENTERICH_LOG_LEVEL. Config mutants such as _Reader.log_level__mutmut_10 survive.
proposal: In test_main.py, set ENTERICH_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR, stub uvicorn.run so that it emits a uvicorn.error warning and error, then run main(). Assert that the captured events are ['start', 'library'] and that the library line is the error.

verdict.reason:
The gap is real, but part of the evidence is wrong.

**The gap.** REQ-002-PRS-NF008 item 6 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:227) says that with `ENTERICH_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR`, the `start` and `rejection` lines are still written and library lines below error are not.
- The only test of the level is tests/unit/test_log.py:50-58 (`test_the_level_filters_library_lines_only`). It calls `log.configure("ERROR", stream)` directly.
- No test sets `ENTERICH_LOG_LEVEL` to a valid value other than the default. I grepped all of tests/, e2e included.
  - tests/unit/test_config.py:43 checks only the default `INFO`.
  - tests/unit/test_config.py:103 checks only that the invalid `TRACE` stops Enterich.
  - tests/unit/test_main.py never sets the variable.
- So nothing checks that `Reader.log_level` (src/enterich/config.py:206-212) gives back `ERROR` for `ERROR` or `error`, or that `main()` passes `settings.log_level` on (src/enterich/__main__.py:23).
- If `__main__` hard-coded `log.configure("INFO")`, every test would still pass.

**The evidence that doesn't hold.** `_Reader.log_level__mutmut_10` changes the default `"INFO"` to `"info"` before `.upper()`, so it is an equivalent mutant. Mutants 23 and 24 change the return after `self.fail`, and that value is thrown away once `load` raises on the problem, so they are equivalent too. None of them supports the gap. Mutants that break the variable name are already killed by the `TRACE` case, so the read path is only partly unchecked.

**Class.** This is a fix within the current specs. The proposed test in tests/unit/test_main.py works:
1. Set `ENTERICH_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR`.
2. Stub `uvicorn.run` so that it logs a warning and an error on `uvicorn.error`. This happens after `log.configure`, and stdout is captured by capsys, as the existing tests already rely on.
3. Run `main()` and assert the events are `['start', 'library']`, with the library line being the error.

Adding a lowercase value such as `error` would also check the `.upper()` normalisation.

claim: Only one direction is tested: that every name in KNOWN is in the guide. 'The code reads no other' is not tested. A _Reader call for a name missing from KNOWN would be both read and reported as an unknown, ignored variable, and the guide test would not require it to be documented.
evidence: tests/repo/test_configuration_guide.py iterates over KNOWN only. No test records which ENTERICH_ names load() reads.
proposal: Add a unit test that passes load() a Mapping subclass recording every key looked up. Assert that the recorded names, minus the prefix, are a subset of KNOWN. Optionally also assert that every `ENTERICH_` name in docs/guides/configuration.md is in KNOWN.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. REQ-002-PRS-NF005's DoD (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:173) says "The configuration guide lists every variable; the code reads no other." Two tests cover the first half. tests/repo/test_configuration_guide.py:9 loops over KNOWN and checks each name is in the guide. tests/repo/test_server_json.py:62-63 checks that the guide's rows, server.json and KNOWN are the same set, so the finding's optional "guide names are in KNOWN" part is already covered by the table rows. Nothing in tests/ (unit, repo or e2e) checks which names load() actually reads: the only other KNOWN/unknown references are the ENTERICH_TOOL warning tests (tests/unit/test_config.py:162, tests/unit/test_main.py:61). I made a mutant in a scratch copy of src/enterich/config.py:127 that also reads an unknown variable (`reader.optional("COMPANYX", "") or reader.text("COMPANY")`). tests/unit/test_config.py plus tests/repo still passed (154 passed). A throwaway test in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/v005/test_reads.py passes on the real code and fails on the mutant. One correction to the proposal: a recording Mapping passed to load() would not see the reads. _Reader.__init__ (config.py:150) copies env through items() into a plain dict, and every lookup after that (get, [], in) goes to self.env. The test therefore has to wrap _Reader.env after construction, for example by monkeypatching _Reader.__init__ to swap self.env for a dict subclass that records get/__getitem__/__contains__. It then asserts that the recorded names are non-empty and a subset of KNOWN. That test needs no spec or code change, so it stays within the current specs.

claim: The test asserts only the status codes. A second process that answered tools/list with a JSON-RPC error inside a 200 would pass, and the test adds little to test_initialize_and_list_tools, which already sends tools/list without a session ID.
evidence: It checks `initialize(first, ...).status_code == 200` and `list_tools(second, ...).status_code == 200`. It does not look at the body or check that no mcp-session-id header was issued.
proposal: Assert offered(response.json()) == list(names()) for the second process, and assert that the initialize response carries no mcp-session-id header.

verdict.reason:
The finding is refuted. Its literal observation is true: tests/integration/test_service.py:100-104 checks only the two status codes. But the behaviour it says goes unchecked is already asserted elsewhere. Every `client(jwks)` builds a new app, which stands in for a fresh process (tests/integration/mcp.py:23-31). test_the_origin_header_changes_nothing (test_service.py:79-97) sends tools/list under 2025-11-25 to a fresh app, with no initialize and no session ID, and asserts `offered(...) == list(names())`. So a process that answered a sessionless tools/list with a JSON-RPC error inside a 200 would fail that test. The same goes for every Session-based integration and e2e test, which call tools/list and tools/call with no initialize (mcp.py:49-85).

The proposed check that no mcp-session-id header is issued is not in the DoD. REQ-002-PRS-NF003's DoD (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:144) asks only that "two requests to different Enterich processes ... succeed in sequence without an MCP session", and the real regression it guards against is already caught. I ran the service tests on a scratch copy with `stateless_http=False` (src/enterich/app.py:61). The SDK then issues a session and answers the sessionless tools/list with 400, and 4 tests fail: test_no_session_state_between_processes itself, test_initialize_and_list_tools (both revisions) and test_the_origin_header_changes_nothing. Adding body and header assertions to this test would only repeat coverage that already exists.

claim: The two-company check is only partial: the assigned company's Item Default row is always the last row in the fixture, so a get_item that ignores the company and takes the last row (or merges the rows in order, the later one winning) still passes.
evidence: tests/integration/test_master_data.py::test_get_item_returns_the_assigned_companys_defaults_only (lines 150-177) uses tests/fakes/erpnext.py::item (lines 1167-1184), where 'Other AG' comes first and COMPANY second. No test puts the assigned company's row first or reverses the order. src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:64 is the only place that picks by company, and a mutant like `rows_of(doc, 'item_defaults')[-1]` would survive every test.
proposal: Parametrize the test over both row orders (assigned company first, then last), giving each row different accounts and cost centres, and assert all four fields equal the assigned company's values and none of the other company's values appear anywhere in the result.

verdict.reason: I couldn't refute it. src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:64 picks the Item Default row by company (`next(... if r.get("company") == company)`). The only test that covers it is tests/integration/test_master_data.py:150-177, and it uses the fixture tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1167-1184, which always puts "Other AG" first and COMPANY last. Line 181 only covers an empty `item_defaults`. Nothing else under tests/ sets item_defaults: tests/e2e/test_master_data.py:15-21 checks only item_code, the flags and the url, and the e2e seed sets no item defaults. To check, I took a scratch copy of HEAD (git archive), swapped line 64 for `defaults = (rows_of(doc, "item_defaults") or [None])[-1]`, and ran tests/integration/test_master_data.py: all 43 tests passed. So a get_item that ignores the company passes, and the REQ-003-PRS-F001 DoD (only the assigned company's accounts and cost centres from an item with rows for two companies) is only partly tested. Closing it needs only a test, which fits the current spec: give the assigned company's row first (or both orders) with values that differ from the other row's, and assert the four default fields. No change to specs, ADRs or code is needed.

claim: The test uses item_defaults=[], so it never runs the company filter: an item whose only Item Default row belongs to another company is untested, and the two cost-centre fields are not checked.
evidence: Line 181 passes `item_defaults=[]`, and line 183 checks only income_account and expense_account. Code that skips the company check and returns the first row would still pass, because the list is empty.
proposal: Seed an item whose only Item Default row is for 'Other AG' and assert that income_account, expense_account, selling_cost_center and buying_cost_center are all None, and that none of the 'OT' values appear in the result.

verdict.reason: I'm rejecting this finding. Its main evidence, that "code that skips the company check and returns the first row would still pass", is false for the test suite. The default item() fixture (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1167-1184) puts the 'Other AG' row (all values ending in OT) first and the assigned company's row (EX) second. tests/integration/test_master_data.py::test_get_item_returns_the_assigned_companys_defaults_only (around lines 149-178) checks the whole result for equality, including all four DEFAULT_FIELDS with their EX values. So the company filter at src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:64 is exercised, and so are both cost-centre fields. That test is exactly the DoD case in REQ-003-PRS-F001: "An item with Item Default rows for two companies returns only the assigned company's accounts and cost centres." I checked this in a scratch copy outside the repository: I removed the company filter, so the code returns the first row. test_get_item_returns_the_assigned_companys_defaults_only then failed (1 failed, 42 passed). The run's survivors.jsonl lists no surviving mutant on the defaults line; master_data's survivors are only the get_named field/what strings, the form_url doctype/name and list_items or_filters. The cost-centre fields are not missing either: all four come from one comprehension over DEFAULT_FIELDS, and the main test checks every one. What remains is an item whose only row belongs to another company, which matters only if someone wrote a deliberate fall-back-to-another-row branch. No such code or mutant exists, and the empty-list test already covers the 'no matching row' result of the current next(..., None) code.

claim: The test checks the input name with a substring match and never checks what the message says is missing, so a wrong field label or a missing 'the item' still passes.
evidence: Line 248 asserts `"item_code" in result.text`. Survivors in harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/survivors.jsonl: enterich.tools.master_data.x_get_item__mutmut_15 (field='XXitem_codeXX', which still contains 'item_code') and x_get_item__mutmut_6 (what=None gives 'item_code: None 'SKU-1' doesn't exist...'), plus the message-filtered mutmut_17 and mutmut_18.
proposal: Assert that the message starts with "item_code: the item 'SKU-1' doesn't exist, or the agent user isn't permitted to read it" (or match it with a regex anchored at `^item_code:`).

verdict.reason:
Confirmed for the wrong field label. The rest of the claim is overstated. tests/integration/test_master_data.py:246-250 asserts `result.error`, `"item_code" in result.text`, `"doesn't exist" in result.text` and `"isn't permitted" in result.text`. So the test does check both possible causes, and the claim's "never checks what the message says is missing" is only partly true: what it misses is the "the item" wording. The message is built in src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:184-188 as f"{field}: {what} {name!r} doesn't exist, or the agent user isn't permitted to read it.", with field="item_code" and what="the item" passed from src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:62.

Mutant x_get_item__mutmut_15 (field="XXitem_codeXX") produces "XXitem_codeXX: the item 'SKU-1' ...". The substring check still passes, yet the message names an input that doesn't exist. That breaks REQ-001-PRS-F009 ("name the input", docs/specs/req-001-core.md:312). The finding cites REQ-003-PRS-F001, but this is the requirement that actually applies.

No other test kills it. tests/e2e/test_rights.py:97-101 matches only the tail of the message ("doesn't exist, or the agent user isn't permitted to read it.$"), and tests/e2e/test_master_data.py has no get_item refusal case. Other integration tests already anchor the field name with `result.text.startswith("<field>:")`, for example test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:225 and test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:275, so a fix within the current specs is to anchor this one too: `result.text.startswith("item_code: ")`, or the full message.

Mutant mutmut_6 (what=None) still names the input and both causes. REQ-001-PRS-F009 doesn't require the words "the item", so that part of the gap is wording only, as are mutmut_17 and mutmut_18, which the harness already filtered as "message". A full-message assertion would kill them too, but they don't justify the fix on their own.

claim: The only test against a real ERPNext never checks item_tax_templates or the company defaults, so a real site that names or hides the Item Tax or Item Default child tables differently from the fake would go unnoticed.
evidence: Lines 15-22 assert only item_code, is_stock_item, disabled and url. The seed (tests/e2e/seed.py:206-222) creates SKU-3 and SKU-4 with item tax templates, but no e2e test reads them through get_item. SKU-1 is seeded with no Item Default row for the company.
proposal: In the e2e suite, call get_item for seeded.item_taxed_19 and assert item_tax_templates contains ITEM_TAX_19. Seed an Item Default row for the assigned company on one item and assert its income_account and selling_cost_center come back.

verdict.reason: The facts are right, but the failure the finding describes can't happen or is already accepted in the spec. The facts: tests/e2e/test_master_data.py:15-22 asserts only item_code, is_stock_item, disabled and url. No e2e test reads item_tax_templates or the company defaults through get_item. The seed (tests/e2e/seed.py:206-222) gives SKU-1 no Item Default row. The failure scenario does not hold up, for three reasons. (1) Child-table names: `item_defaults` and `taxes` are fixed fieldnames in ERPNext's own Item DocType, and a site cannot rename a standard fieldname. The fake uses exactly these names (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:257). The `taxes` name is also already checked against a real site: the seed writes `taxes=[{item_tax_template: ...}]` to SKU-3 and SKU-4 over REST, and tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py:108,143-144 and tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:135-223 only pass if ERPNext stored and applied those templates. (2) The path that fetches the rows is already covered end to end: get_item uses get_named -> erpnext.get_doc (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:191-207), which is frappe.client.get. REQ-001 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:642-644) lists 'frappe.client.get for a document with its rows' as checked by the e2e test, and the invoice e2e tests read child rows through it. Mapping the rows (src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:61-79) is pinned by tests/integration/test_master_data.py:150-200, including the DoD case of two companies' Item Default rows. (3) Hidden rows: a field above the agent's permission level comes back as null. REQ-001 puts this under 'Not checked yet' as the deployment's job, and says 'a get can't tell it from an empty one' (docs/specs/req-001-core.md, Not checked yet list), so no e2e assertion can catch it within the current specs. What is left is a small confidence gain on the standard `item_defaults` fieldname. That is not worth seeding an Item Default row and adding e2e assertions.

claim: No end-to-end test checks the Accounts Receivable columns `age` and `posting_date` against ERPNext v16. If either name is wrong, `aged_report` quietly returns None for it.
evidence: src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py aged_report builds each record with `{f: row.get(f) for f in side.aged_fields}`, so a missing column gives None and no error. tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py::test_accounts_receivable_ages_the_open_part_by_due_date asserts voucher_type, voucher_no, party, invoiced, paid, credit_note, outstanding, due_date, currency and ageing, but not `age` or `posting_date`. test_accounts_receivable_as_of_today_by_default asserts neither. A grep of tests/e2e finds no assertion on a report row's `age` or `posting_date`. The integration test test_report_rows_are_records_without_the_total_row checks them only against the fake's receivable() row (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1316), whose column names are the fake author's guess.
proposal: In test_accounts_receivable_ages_the_open_part_by_due_date, also assert `record["posting_date"] == seeded.posted.isoformat()` and `record["age"] == 0` (as of the posting date, by due date: ERPNext's age column for that ageing basis). Assert a non-None `age` in the as-of-today test too.

verdict.reason: The gap is real. src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:297 builds each record with `{f: row.get(f) for f in side.aged_fields}`, so a wrong column name comes back as None with no error. The receivable side's aged_fields (src/enterich/tools/order_to_cash.py:72-84) include `posting_date` and `age`. In tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py, test_accounts_receivable_ages_the_open_part_by_due_date (around line 222) asserts voucher_type, voucher_no, party, invoiced, paid, credit_note, outstanding, due_date, currency, ageing and total_outstanding. It never asserts `age` or `posting_date`. test_accounts_receivable_as_of_today_by_default and test_accounts_receivable_as_of_the_day_before_shows_nothing assert neither. I grepped all of tests/ for `"age"` and for report_accounts_receivable. The only `age` assertions are in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:483 and tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay.py:325, and both check against the fake rows (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1333, 1473). No test in tests/repo or harness/ checks the column names. REQ-004-PRS-F004's DoD says "Report filters and columns match ERPNext v16", with the end-to-end test as evidence, so this is required behaviour that can be observed, and closing it needs only a test. The class is fix. One correction to the proposal: `age == 0` is probably wrong. With ageing by due date and the report run as of the posting date, ERPNext's age is report_date minus due_date, which is negative while the invoice is not yet due. That fits the test putting the amount in range0, "not yet due". The test should assert `record["age"] == (seeded.posted - seeded.sales_due).days` and `record["posting_date"] == seeded.posted.isoformat()`. If unsure of the sign, it can at least assert `age` is an int and not None. The same gap exists for `age` on the payable side (test_accounts_payable_by_posting_date, src/enterich/tools/procure_to_pay.py:95). There, ageing by posting date as of the posting date should give age 0.

claim: On a fresh site the seeded invoice is posted today, so no test checks that a past `as_of_date` ages rows from that date rather than from today. Only a site kept past the due date checks it.
evidence: tests/e2e/seed.py Vouchers.__init__ sets `posted = site_today()` on a fresh site, so the as_of_date=seeded.posted call in tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py::test_accounts_receivable_ages_the_open_part_by_due_date is not in the past there. test_accounts_receivable_as_of_the_day_before_shows_nothing uses a past date but checks only that the result is empty. The integration test test_the_report_call_carries_the_given_inputs pins the `age_as_on` filter, but the fake computes no ageing.
proposal: Add an e2e test with a submitted sales invoice posted well in the past (e.g. 90 days ago, due 30 days later; seed it with set_posting_time). Report it with as_of_date = its posting date and assert its outstanding sits in range0 with age 0, not in the bucket ageing from today would give (range2).

verdict.reason: I couldn't refute this finding. REQ-004-PRS-F004's DoD item 2 (docs/specs/req-004-order-to-cash.md:99) requires that "an `as_of_date` in the past ages the rows from that date, not from today", and line 102 names the e2e test against a real ERPNext v16 site as its evidence. On a fresh site, which is what CI uses (.github/workflows/e2e.yml:29 runs scripts/erpnext-site.sh up, then pytest tests/e2e), the seed posts every submitted voucher today: tests/e2e/seed.py:523 sets `self.posted = site_today()`. So tests/e2e/test_invoicing.py:212 (test_accounts_receivable_ages_the_open_part_by_due_date) calls the report with as_of_date=seeded.posted, which is today and not a past date. Its range0 assertion would pass even if ERPNext aged from today. test_accounts_receivable_as_of_the_day_before_shows_nothing (test_invoicing.py:271) does use a past date, but it only asserts an empty result, so no ageing is checked. test_accounts_receivable_as_of_today_by_default (line 238) checks only that the ageing buckets add up to 69. On the Enterich side, tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:436-461 pins `report_date` to the given date and `age_as_on: "Report Date"` (src/enterich/tools/invoicing.py:284-287), so a mutant of those filters would die. But the fake ERPNext computes no ageing, so nothing checks that ERPNext v16 actually ages from report_date. That is exactly what the e2e evidence is for. Only a kept site past the 30-day due date would check it today. I searched tests/e2e for timedelta and days=: no other past-dated voucher exists. A test closes this within the current specs: seed a separate submitted sales invoice posted in the past with set_posting_time, report it as of a past date and assert its bucket. Two cautions for the fix. First, give it its own customer, or it changes the single-record assertions for seeded.customer. Second, seed.py:195 only makes the fiscal year for site_today().year, so a voucher 90 days back needs that year's fiscal year too, or a date that stays inside the current year. No spec, ADR or dependency change is needed.

claim: The rule that a create with `items` sends only the rows of the given items is checked only against invoices whose other items have nothing left to return.
evidence: In tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py::test_a_create_sends_erpnexts_return_with_the_given_items and test_a_create_returns_the_draft, the left-out item SKU-2 (r2) was already fully returned by ACC-SINV-2026-00002. The free-item and 0.3/0.1 tests and BILL each hold only SKU-1. The fixed-amount test's partial case is refused before any rows are sent. A version that also sent unnamed items with quantity left (skipping 0) would pass every test.
proposal: Add a test against an invoice of two items that both have quantity left (e.g. SKU-1 at 2 and SKU-2 at 1, none returned). Create with items=[SKU-1 qty 1] and assert the POST body's items == lines(mapped, (0, 1)), with no SKU-2 row.

verdict.reason: The gap is real, and closing it needs only a test. REQ-004-PRS-F007's DoD item 1 (docs/specs/req-004-order-to-cash.md:138) requires that a create with `items` "sends only the rows of the given items". src/enterich/tools/returns.py rows() (lines 151-175) does this correctly today, but no test catches a change to it. In the fixture (tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:26, 69-86) the left-out SKU-2 row r2 was already fully returned by ACC-SINV-2026-00002. The tests at :191, :224 and :443 all build on that invoice; :649 only checks there is no error. The free-item, 0.3/0.1 and BILL tests hold only SKU-1. The fixed-amount test (:617) is refused before any write. The e2e tests (tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:533-600) use a single seeded item. I applied a mutant in a scratch copy of the repo: after the items loop it appends the unnamed rows that still have quantity left, without counting them in `returned`. All 884 unit and integration tests passed on it. I then added a throwaway test: an invoice with v1 SKU-1 at 2 and v2 SKU-2 at 1, nothing returned, created with items=[SKU-1 qty 1], asserting post.body["items"] == lines(mapped, (0, 1)). It fails on the mutant and passes on the original code. It uses only the existing invoice() and lines() helpers, so no change to the specs, ADRs or code is needed.

claim: A return above what is left must be refused naming `items`, the item and the quantity left. No test asserts that the refusal names the item.
evidence: In tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py::test_items_are_returned_at_most_as_far_as_left, the cases SKU-1 qty 5 and SKU-2 qty 1 assert only "4 left" / "0 left" plus the `items: ` prefix, not SKU-1 or SKU-2. test_an_update_beyond_what_is_left_is_refused asserts only the prefix `items: ` and no write. tests/e2e/test_drafts.py::test_a_return_above_what_is_left_is_refused asserts only "2 left". The message in src/enterich/tools/returns.py rows() could lose the item code and every test would still pass.
proposal: In the above-left cases, assert that the item code appears in the text alongside the quantity left (e.g. "of SKU-1 can't be returned; 4 left"). In the update test, also assert "SKU-1" and "4 left".

verdict.reason: The spec requires it: docs/specs/req-004-order-to-cash.md line 144 (REQ-004-PRS-F007 DoD) says an item returned above what is left "is refused naming `items`, the item and the quantity left". The code does name the item. src/enterich/tools/returns.py:161-163 raises `items: {qty} of {item_code} can't be returned; {left} left to return on {name}.`. No test checks the item name, though. tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:277-278 (the SKU-1 qty 5 and SKU-2 qty 1 cases of test_items_are_returned_at_most_as_far_as_left, lines 282-289) asserts only the `items: ` prefix and "4 left" / "0 left", and neither substring contains the item code. test_an_update_beyond_what_is_left_is_refused (lines 486-490) asserts only the prefix and that nothing was written. tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:566-573 asserts only the prefix and "2 left". I grepped all of tests/ for an item-code assertion on these refusal texts and found none. The only item-naming assertion is "SKU-9 isn't on", and that covers the item-not-on-invoice branch, not the above-left one. So if the message dropped `{item.item_code}`, every test would still pass. claim: Nothing tells Enterich's own decimal sums of the root rows apart from ERPNext's float total row, or from a float sum. The 'as decimals' and 'Enterich's sums' parts of the item go unchecked, and so does summing over every account rather than only the shown page.

The e2e test_trial_balance_of_the_year only checks debit == credit > 0.

Make the fake's total row differ from the true sum, for example by setting it to a wrong value. Assert totals.debit == 0.3. Call it with limit=1 and assert that totals still cover every root row.

verdict.reason:
The gap is real: the only test that checks Trial Balance totals cannot tell Enterich's decimal sums apart from ERPNext's total row, from a float sum, or from a sum over the shown page only.

What the spec requires: docs/specs/req-006-record-to-report.md:98 says "`totals` are Enterich's sums over the root accounts' rows, as decimals".

How the code does it: src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:470-473 sums `decimal(...)` over every root in `accounts`. The page `shown` (line 474) is cut only after that.

Why the test misses it: tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py:533 (test_trial_balance_rows_and_totals) uses balances() (lines 484-493). Each total there comes from one root with a value and one root at 0.0: debit 0.3+0.0, credit 0.0+0.3, opening 1000+0, closing 1000.3+0.0. In Python, 1000.0+0.3 == 1000.3 and 0.3+0.0 == 0.3, so every float sum is exact. The fake's balance_total (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:1687) is a float sum over the same roots, so it equals the asserted totals too. The comment on line 559 ("not ERPNext's float total") is wrong for this data.

These three mutants all pass:
- totals taken from rows[-1] (ERPNext's total row);
- a float sum instead of a decimal one;
- a sum over `shown` instead of all accounts. The default limit is 20 (record_to_report.py:271) and there are only 4 rows, so the page holds every row.

Nothing else in tests/ checks these totals:
- The other `totals` asserts (lines 327 and 359) are for the General Ledger.
- The e2e test tests/e2e/test_record_to_report.py:103-113 only checks debit == credit > 0 and closing_debit == closing_credit.

Why it is a fix: a new integration test closes it within the current spec. It needs two roots whose float sum is inexact (0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004), a fake total row set apart from the true sum, an assert that totals.debit == 0.3, and a call with limit=1 asserting that totals still cover every root. No change to the specs or ADRs is needed.

verdict.reason:
