verdict.reason:
I'm treating this as refuted because the behaviour can't be observed. The mutant does survive: `mutmut show enterich.shapes.x_rows_of__mutmut_4` reports "survived". It is also not equivalent: given a dict without the key, it returns None where the original returns [], and `cut_rows(None)` at src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:239 would raise.

But the else branch of rows_of (src/enterich/shapes.py:154-157) never runs against the ERPNext the specs target. The specs name ERPNext v16 (for example docs/specs/req-004-order-to-cash.md:100, docs/specs/req-006-record-to-report.md:84). Gets go through `frappe.client.get` (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:606), and writes through `/api/resource`. Both answer with Frappe's `doc.as_dict()`, which as I understand Frappe's code writes every table field as `self.get(fieldname) or []`. So a catalogued child table always arrives as a list, empty or not. That holds even after `apply_fieldlevel_read_permissions` sets a field the user may not read to None. I worked this from my reading of Frappe, not from running a v16 site.

The fake in tests/fakes/erpnext.py models that answer. Its `frappe.client.get` handler (lines 433-437) returns the stored document unchanged, and its fixtures, such as the Item at line 1154 with `item_defaults`, always include their tables. That is why no test reaches the else branch. The proposed integration test would need the fake to send something v16 doesn't, which goes against the fake's job of modelling v16.

No spec requires behaviour for a missing table: REQ-001-PRS-NF003 (req-001-core.md:541) and the get shape (req-001-core.md:583) only describe tables ERPNext sends. Only the docstring states the [] fallback, so the branch is defensive.

A one-line unit test, `rows_of({}, 'items') == []`, would kill the mutant, but it would only pin a guard against an input ERPNext can't send. I didn't write the throwaway test, because the mutant's diff alone shows it returns None for a missing key. If the triage disagrees and wants the gap closed anyway, that unit test in tests/unit/test_shapes.py is the whole fix, within the current specs.

claim: The `operation` line's level is never checked: refusals logged at INFO, every outcome at WARNING, or the levels swapped all pass.

The tests that do read `operation` lines (tests/unit/test_tools.py:69,98,110,119,152, tests/integration/test_master_data.py:323, tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:601-703, tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:78) check only the operation, outcome, call and arguments fields. The mutants mutmut showed are not equivalent: _19 drops the level argument, so the default INFO applies; _32 adds `and False`; _36 swaps the condition to `not in`. Each changes the level a refused or a successful call is logged at. The survivors also include _33, _34 and _35 (harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/survivors.jsonl). I wrote a throwaway test in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/lvl19/test_level_scratch.py. A test can pin the current behaviour without breaking any spec or ADR. ADR-008:17 counts this kind of survivor (the `ensure_ascii` example) as a real gap that a test closes. If the operator wants the warning-for-refusal rule to be part of the contract, the extra step would be one sentence in REQ-002-PRS-NF008, which makes it a proposal.

claim: The cutting of a long refusal is tested only as '<= 300', so a refusal of exactly 300 characters cut needlessly, or a cut to 299 characters, both pass.

proposal: Unit test of _refused (or through an operation raising Refusal): a 300-character text comes back unchanged; a 301-character text comes back as exactly 300 characters ending in '…', and the logged outcome's refusal is the same text.

verdict.reason: I couldn't refute the finding. In src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:321-324, `_refused` cuts a text only when `len(text) > MAX_MESSAGE` (300), keeping `text[:299] + "…"`, and puts the same text in the logged outcome. `mutmut show` reports both mutants as survived: mutmut_1 changes `>` to `>=`, and mutmut_5 changes `MAX_MESSAGE - 1` to `- 2`. Neither mutant is equivalent, and the agent would see the difference. Under mutmut_1, a refusal of exactly 300 characters loses its last character to "…". Under mutmut_5, a refusal over 300 characters comes back as 299 characters. I searched all of tests/ (unit, integration, e2e) and no test asserts the exact cut. The closest tests check only an upper bound: tests/unit/test_tools.py:97 and :151/:157 check `len(text) <= 300`, tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:172 does the same, and tests/integration/test_master_data.py:260 and :267 check `<= 300`. No test outside tests/readme.py contains "…". REQ-001-PRS-F008 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:294-307) asks only for "at most 300 characters", so both mutants still meet the spec. Even so, cutting a refusal that already fits throws away part of it, and the agent sees that. A unit test can pin the exact cut within the current specs: a 300-character Refusal comes back unchanged, and a 301-character one comes back as exactly 300 characters ending in "…", with outcome["refusal"] equal to the text. The existing `call` helper in tests/unit/test_tools.py can carry both cases, and no spec or ADR change is needed.

claim: No test checks that non-ASCII text reaches the agent as it is: with ensure_ascii on, 'Müller' becomes 'Müller', which makes the result longer (so it hits the 100,000 limit sooner) and harder to read, and nothing notices.
evidence: enterich.shapes.x_to_text__mutmut_6 (ensure_ascii removed) and enterich.shapes.x_to_text__mutmut_8 (ensure_ascii=True). (x_to_text__mutmut_3, ensure_ascii=None, is equivalent because None is falsy.)
proposal: Unit test: to_text({"customer_name": "Müller €"}) contains 'Müller €' literally and no '\\u'; optionally an integration get of a customer with a non-ASCII name whose result text contains the name unescaped.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. src/enterich/shapes.py:224 calls `json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, default=_number)`, and both tools/__init__.py:305 and :317 use it to build the result text that reaches the agent and is checked against the 100,000-character limit. `mutmut show` reports x_to_text__mutmut_6 (ensure_ascii dropped) as survived, and mutmut_8 (ensure_ascii=True) is the same change. I searched all of tests/, tests/e2e included, and found no assertion on the raw result text containing non-ASCII. Some tests do use non-ASCII data: 'Hauptstraße 1' in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:149 and 'Eröffnung' in test_record_to_report.py:422. But they compare `.data`, which is `json.loads(self.text)` (tests/integration/mcp.py:46). Parsing reverses the \u escapes, so these tests pass with or without the mutant. 'Müller GmbH' in tests/unit/test_shapes.py:63 only checks name validation. The e2e text checks in test_language.py are ASCII and test refusals, which don't go through to_text. The behaviour can be seen from outside: the agent receives different text, and the length counted against REQ-001's limit (req-001-core.md:541) changes, with up to 6 characters per non-ASCII character. ADR-008:17 itself names this exact survivor as a real gap. I ran a scratch check: to_text({"customer_name": "Müller €"}) gives text containing 'Müller €' and no '\u'. Plain json.dumps, which is what the mutant does, gives 'Müller €'. So the proposed unit test kills both mutants. It is a test only, within the current specs, and needs no code change.

claim: A get's `url` is never tested with ERPNext returning a name spelled differently from the input (ERPNext's lookup ignores case), so building the link from the input name instead of the document's name passes.
evidence: enterich.tools.x_get_document__mutmut_57 (`doc.get(None, name)`), _61 ("XXnameXX"), _62 ("NAME"): each always uses the input name. In every test the fake returns the requested name unchanged. (_58 and _60 differ only when the document has no `name`, which ERPNext never sends: equivalent.)
proposal: Integration test: get_customer with name 'acme' where the fake ERPNext returns the document with name 'ACME'; assert the url ends in '/desk/customer/ACME'.

verdict.reason: The gap is real, but the proposed test is aimed at the wrong tool. src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:247 builds the url from `doc.get("name", name)`. Mutants _57, _61 and _62 change that key to None, "XXnameXX" and "NAME", so the url always uses the input name. The only test that serves a document under a name in different case is tests/integration/test_master_data.py:218 (test_the_url_uses_the_name_erpnext_answers_with). It calls get_item, and get_item builds its own url at src/enterich/tools/master_data.py:74 without going through get_document. The callers of get_document are get_invoice (invoicing.py:238), the two bank_and_cash.py gets (lines 281 and 319) and the record_to_report.py get (line 346). Their url tests (for example tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:319, test_bank_and_cash.py:284/428, test_record_to_report.py:254) all request the stored name exactly, so they cannot tell the mutants apart. No test in tests/e2e covers this either. The behaviour is required: REQ-001 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:586) says the url is the document's form and carries the name. The code and the item test show the stored name is intended, since ERPNext finds names case-insensitively. Correction: the proposal's get_customer goes through get_party (invoicing.py:125-153), not get_document, so it would not kill these mutants. The fix should be the same aliasing test as the item one, on a get_document caller. For example, alias erp.docs["Sales Invoice"]["acc-sinv-2026-00001"] to the stored invoice, call the sales invoice get with the lowercase name, and assert the url ends in /desk/sales-invoice/ACC-SINV-2026-00001. This stays within the current specs; no code change is needed. I did not run a throwaway test against the mutants; the conclusion comes from reading the code and the tests.

claim: No test updates an invoice draft whose posting date is fixed (set_posting_time 1) and lies before today without giving a date, so dropping the set_posting_time check, which then empties the payment schedule and recounts a due date that should stay, goes unnoticed.
evidence: enterich.tools.drafts.x_due_dates__mutmut_12, _13, _14 (stored.get(None) / misspelt key, so `not ...` is always True). test_an_update_without_a_date_keeps_the_due_date (tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py) uses a draft created today, so `posting_date != today` is already False; test_a_floating_draft_can_be_updated_on_a_later_day covers only set_posting_time 0.
proposal: Add a draft with set_posting_time 1, posting_date 2026-10-01 and a due_date, update it with remarks only, and assert that the PUT body is exactly {remarks, modified} (no payment_schedule, no due_date) and that the due date is kept. Parametrize it over sales and purchase invoices.

verdict.reason:
The gap is real. src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:195 computes `moves = not stored.get("set_posting_time") and stored.get("posting_date") != str(day)`. Mutant x_due_dates__mutmut_12 (checked with mutmut show; it survived) turns this into `stored.get(None)`, so `moves` becomes just `posting_date != today`. The mutant only changes the result for a stored draft with set_posting_time 1 and a posting date other than today, updated without due_date, posting_date or bill_date. In that case it adds `payment_schedule: []` and `due_date: None` to the PUT body.

No test covers that case:
- The default update draft in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:82-88 and tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:60-72 uses set_posting_time 0 with posting_date TODAY.
- test_an_update_without_a_date_keeps_the_due_date (test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:1029) updates a draft created today without a posting date.
- test_a_floating_draft_can_be_updated_on_a_later_day (line 1012) uses set_posting_time 0.
- The other set_posting_time 1 cases are create bodies (line 135), updates that give posting_date (lines 724, 1005), and return drafts.
- tests/e2e has no update of a fixed-date draft without a date. test_drafts.py:255 is a create-side duplicate check.

The behaviour is required. REQ-001-PRS-F017 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:425) limits the schedule reset to drafts whose posting date is not fixed (set_posting_time 0) and not today. Its DoD (line 435) says an update that gives no date, of a draft whose posting date stays, sends no schedule and keeps the due date. A fixed posting date in the past is such a draft. The mutant is not equivalent, because the PUT body changes, and the existing tests already compare that body exactly.

The proposed test closes the gap within the current specs: add a set_posting_time 1 draft with posting_date 2026-10-01 and a due_date, update only remarks, and assert the body is exactly {remarks, modified} and the due date is kept, for both sales and purchase invoices. I did not write a throwaway test to run against the mutant; the conclusion rests on the mutmut diff and the existing exact-body asserts.

claim: The duplicate match treats items as a multiset, but no test has a draft with two identical rows, so counting each (item, qty) only once goes unnoticed. That refuses a create of [SKU-1×1] against a draft holding [SKU-1×1, SKU-1×1], and misses the real duplicate when both have two identical rows.
evidence: enterich.tools.drafts.x_duplicates__mutmut_51 (`found[...] += 1` -> `= 1`). The duplicate tests in test_order_to_cash_drafts.py and test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py use drafts with distinct item rows. REQ-005-PRS-F006 states the same match for purchase invoices.
proposal: Add a draft with items [SKU-1 qty 1, SKU-1 qty 1]. Assert that a create with one SKU-1 qty 1 row goes through without a warning, and that a create with two such rows is refused naming the draft.

So the match treats items as a multiset, as REQ-004-PRS-F006 and REQ-005-PRS-F006 require ("same items (item codes and quantities, in any order)"; the DoD says a create matching a draft is refused and one differing in a quantity goes through). `mutmut show` reports enterich.tools.drafts.x_duplicates__mutmut_51 (`+= 1` -> `= 1`) as survived, and it is listed in harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/survivors.jsonl:563. No test in tests/ has a draft with two identical rows in a duplicate check. The `* 21` at tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:252 is the 21-row limit refusal. tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:279 covers returns, which don't call drafts.duplicates. The duplicate tests at test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:305-375 all use distinct rows. I wrote a throwaway test at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/t/test_multiset.py, reusing the repo fixtures. It ran against the original code and against a copy with the mutation applied, at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/mut. claim: The spec says a given amount matches a stored one that differs by at most 0.005, but the only rounding test differs by 0.004. So changing `<=` to `<` slips through, and a repeat of 100.005 (ERPNext stores 100.0 or 100.01) is no longer caught as a duplicate.
evidence: enterich.tools.record_to_report.x__same_rows__mutmut_13 (debit `<`), x__same_rows__mutmut_18 (credit `<`). test_a_repeated_create_matches_the_amounts_erpnext_rounded uses 100.004, saved as 100.0.
proposal: Parametrize test_a_repeated_create_matches_the_amounts_erpnext_rounded with rows of debit 100.005 / credit 100.005, which the fake saves rounded to two places, a difference of exactly 0.005. Assert the second create is refused naming the first draft. One case with both a debit and a credit row kills both mutants.

verdict.reason: The gap is real, and one test inside the current specs closes it. src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:553 compares each amount with `<= ROUNDING` (ROUNDING = Decimal("0.005") at line 115). Searching tests/ (unit, integration, e2e) found no other test of the duplicate match at the 0.005 boundary. `mutmut show` lists mutant 13 (debit `<`) as survived and shows mutant 18 as the matching credit `<`. The fake rounds with float round() (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:780-781), so 100.005 is stored as 100.0, while Enterich keeps Decimal("100.005"). Check: I copied src/ and tests/ to scratchpad/verify-same-rows-5a1c and added the proposed case (debit 100.005 / credit 100.005, second create refused naming the first draft). claim: The spec says rows match the given ones in the order given, but no test has rows whose given values differ in a way a warning depends on. So pairing row n with given row n-1 (row 1 with the last) goes unnoticed: such a warning names the wrong given rate or account, or doesn't appear at all.
evidence: enterich.tools.drafts.x_row_warnings__mutmut_31 (`given[number - 2]`). The single-row tests and test_the_cap_counts_rows_not_warnings (15 identical rows) can't tell the pairing apart. The same pairing drives REQ-005-PRS-F007's expense-account warning.
proposal: Create an invoice with rows [SKU-1 rate 48 (a pricing rule saves 45), SKU-2 rate 20 (kept)]. Assert exactly one warning, for row 1, naming 48 and 45. Also, for a purchase invoice, give row 2 an expense account ERPNext replaces and row 1 one it keeps, and assert only row 2 warns.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed: the gap is real and can be fixed. In src/enterich/tools/drafts.py:220, row n is matched to its given row with `given[number - 1]`. `mutmut show` reports mutant x_row_warnings__mutmut_31 (`given[number - 2]`) as survived. Every test where rows are given leaves the pairing untested:
- tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py: test_a_rate_a_pricing_rule_replaced_warns, test_kept_rates_and_free_items_dont_warn and test_a_rate_erpnext_only_rounded_doesnt_warn each give one row, and with one row given[-1] is given[0]. test_a_row_without_a_price_warns gives two rows, but the rate-0 warning doesn't read the given row: row 2 has no pricing_rules, so it reaches the rate-0 branch either way.
- tests/integration/test_procure_to_pay_drafts.py:382-411 and tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:379-395 (expense account) give one row only.
- The e2e test of the tax summary (tests/e2e/test_drafts.py:220-243) gives several rows, all at rate 100, and asserts no warnings.

I ran throwaway tests in a scratch copy of the repo (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/repo):

- A purchase invoice with [INK given 4940 (kept), PAPER (stock item) given 4930 (replaced by Stock Received But Not Billed)] asserts a single warning for row 2. It also passes on the original and fails on the mutant. The two rows must be given different accounts; with the same account the mutant survives.

So two integration tests close the gap with no code or spec change, within REQ-001-PRS-F016 and REQ-005-PRS-F007.

claim: No test runs the General Ledger with party_type alone (allowed: only party needs party_type). So the party lookup can run with a None name, which refuses or breaks the call, and no test notices.
evidence: enterich.tools.record_to_report.x_report_general_ledger__mutmut_22 (`and` -> `or`). test_the_ledger_call_carries_the_given_inputs_as_lists and test_unknown_names_are_refused_before_the_report always give party with party_type.
proposal: Call report_general_ledger with only party_type Customer. Assert there is no error, that the report filters carry party_type Customer and no party, and that no Customer get_doc call reached the fake.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. The mutant is a real gap, not an equivalent one, and a test can close it under the current specs.

- **Code:** src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:367 looks up the party only when both `party` and `party_type` are given. Mutant 22 changes the `and` to `or`. The input check at lines 194-195 only refuses `party` without `party_type`, so `party_type` alone is valid input.
- **Spec:** docs/specs/req-006-record-to-report.md:182 says "`party` requires `party_type`", but not the reverse. Line 205 and REQ-006-PRS-F003 (line 73) say to check only a given `party` before the report. So `party_type` alone is allowed, and no lookup should happen for it.
- **Existing tests:** every General Ledger call in tests/ gives `party_type` together with `party`, or leaves both out. That covers tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py:282-470, tests/e2e/test_record_to_report.py:90, tests/e2e/test_language.py:37 and tests/e2e/test_rights.py:150. The `party` without `party_type` case at line 458 only tests the refusal.
- **Check:** I wrote a throwaway test in a scratch copy of the repo, under the session scratchpad. It sets `erp.reports['General Ledger'] = ledger([])` and calls the report with only `party_type` Customer. It asserts no error, no non-report request reaching the fake, and filters with `party_type` Customer and no `party`.
  - On the original code it passed.
  - On the mutant it failed with "party: the customer None doesn't exist, or the agent user isn't permitted to read it."
  - The existing tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py, 38 tests, all passed on the mutant, confirming it survives today.
- **Fix:** the proposed test closes the gap within the current specs; the throwaway test above is that test. No change to the specs or ADRs is needed.

claim: list_accounts, list_cost_centers and list_journal_entries are never tested paging, and their catalogued-call tests don't check limit_start or limit_page_length. So fetching limit-1 rows, which drops the last record and reports has_more false although more exist, goes unnoticed.
evidence: enterich.tools.record_to_report.x__tree__mutmut_41 and x_list_journal_entries__mutmut_43 (page_length limit-1). x__tree__mutmut_42 and x_list_journal_entries__mutmut_44 (limit+2) change only the request and fall to the same assertion. The fake honours limit_page_length (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:907), but test_list_accounts_sends_exactly_the_catalogued_call, test_list_cost_centers_sends_exactly_the_catalogued_call and test_list_journal_entries_sends_exactly_the_catalogued_call assert no paging params.
proposal: In the three catalogued-call tests, call with limit 5 and offset 5 and assert limit_start == '5' and limit_page_length == '6'. Or add a paging test per list, as test_master_data.py does for list_items: limit 1 over 2 records gives count 1 and has_more true.

verdict.reason:
I couldn't refute this finding. `_tree` (src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:306) and `list_journal_entries` (:339) both ask ERPNext for `page_length=inputs.limit + 1` and pass the rows to `page()`. `mutmut show` confirms what the mutants change: `x__tree__mutmut_41` and `x_list_journal_entries__mutmut_43` make it `limit - 1`, and `x__tree__mutmut_42` and `x_list_journal_entries__mutmut_44` make it `limit + 2`. All four are listed in harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/survivors.jsonl. None is equivalent: with `limit - 1`, a call with limit 2 over 3 records returns 1 record and has_more false, which breaks the `has_more` and `count` result convention in REQ-001-PRS-F014 and REQ-001 Operation Conventions (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:385, :581). The `limit + 2` mutants show up only in the request.

I searched all of tests/ and no test catches them. In tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py, the catalogued-call tests for accounts (:103), cost centres (:149) and journal entries (:174) check fields, filters, or_filters and order_by, but never `limit_start` or `limit_page_length`. No test in that file pages these three lists or checks has_more for them; the only has_more check is for the general ledger (:330). tests/e2e/test_record_to_report.py:16-52 only checks records. tests/e2e/test_rights.py:246-248 calls them with default inputs. test_record_to_report_drafts.py only mentions `list_journal_entries` in a description string (:162). The pattern the proposal asks for already exists elsewhere: tests/integration/test_bank_and_cash.py:137 asserts ("5", "6") for limit 5 and offset 5, and tests/integration/test_master_data.py:68-79 has a paging test. So tests alone close the gap within the current specs, with no spec or code change.

I didn't run a throwaway test against the mutants. The finding rests on the survivors file and on reading the tests.

claim: No test pages the Trial Balance, so slicing limit-1 rows instead of limit+1 goes unnoticed: a page then shows one record too few and has_more false although more accounts follow.
evidence: enterich.tools.record_to_report.x_report_trial_balance__mutmut_73 (`+ inputs.limit - 1`). test_trial_balance_rows_and_totals uses the default limit 20 over 4 accounts. x_report_trial_balance__mutmut_75 (+2) and x_report_general_ledger__mutmut_132 (+2) are equivalent, since page() cuts to limit.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. The finding holds. At src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py:474 the code slices `accounts[offset : offset + limit + 1]` and hands the result to page() (src/enterich/shapes.py:191-201). page() works out has_more as len(records) > limit. Mutant 73 (`limit - 1`) therefore gives limit-1 records and always has_more false, so it is not equivalent. The +2 mutants are equivalent, as the finding says, because page() cuts to limit.

The tests at tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py:481-626 all use the default limit over balances()' 4 accounts, and has_more is asserted only at line 330, in the General Ledger's paging test. tests/e2e/test_record_to_report.py:116-130 does page the Trial Balance with limit 100 against a real ERPNext. But pyproject.toml:74 runs mutmut with --ignore=tests/e2e, and whether that test would catch the mutant depends on the order of the seeded chart of accounts. So it doesn't close the gap.

I checked this on a throwaway copy of the repository in the scratchpad, not in the repo. A test with limit 2 asserts count 2, has_more true and the first two accounts, then offset 2 asserts the other two and has_more false. It passes on the real code. With only line 474 mutated, it is the only failure in the full non-e2e suite (1 failed, 884 passed).

Paging (limit, offset, has_more) is already required behaviour for every list and report tool, so the test fits the current specs and needs no spec change. Class: fix.

claim: No record-to-report list or report test checks the result's offset, so returning offset null goes unnoticed in all four operations.
evidence: enterich.tools.record_to_report.x__tree__mutmut_55, x_list_journal_entries__mutmut_53, x_report_general_ledger__mutmut_146, x_report_trial_balance__mutmut_102 (`page(records, None, ...)`). tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py asserts count/has_more (line 330) but never offset.
proposal: Add one test parametrized over list_accounts, list_cost_centers, list_journal_entries, report_general_ledger and report_trial_balance. Call each with offset 1 and assert result['offset'] == 1, along with count and has_more.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. REQ-001-PRS-F014's Definition of Done (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:385) says list and report results carry `offset`. src/enterich/tools/record_to_report.py passes `inputs.offset` to `page()` at four places: line 309 (`_tree`, which list_accounts and list_cost_centers both use), line 342 (list_journal_entries), line 404 (report_general_ledger) and line 486 (report_trial_balance). `page()` in src/enterich/shapes.py:191 copies the value straight into the result.

All four mutants are listed in harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/survivors.jsonl with the diff `page(records, None, ...)`. None is equivalent: the result would show `offset: null` where the spec requires the real number, even 0 in the default case.

No test checks it:
- tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py only asserts `(count, has_more)` (line 330). Its whole-result comparison at line 218 is for get_journal_entry, which is not a list.
- tests/e2e/test_record_to_report.py:120-125 sends its own offset when paging but never reads `report["offset"]`.
- No other test file (test_record_to_report_drafts.py, the e2e rights/language tests, test_tool_list.py, test_service.py) asserts offset for these tools. Only master data (tests/integration/test_master_data.py:44,75) and accounts receivable (tests/integration/test_order_to_cash.py:516) do, for their own tools.

I checked this with a throwaway test outside the repo (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/t/test_offset.py). On a scratch copy with the `_tree` and list_journal_entries mutants applied, it fails with "assert None == 1".

claim: Nothing checks how main() calls uvicorn.run for the app, host, log_config and access_log: dropping log_config=None (uvicorn then applies its own non-JSON LOGGING_CONFIG), turning access logging on (True or None, because uvicorn only switches it off for `is False`), dropping the configured host (uvicorn then listens on 127.0.0.1 instead of ENTERICH_HOST) or passing None as the app all pass the tests.

Checked uvicorn.Config: it calls dictConfig when log_config is not None, and empties the access logger only when `access_log is False`; log.configure turns propagation back on for uvicorn.access, so access lines would show up as `library` lines.
proposal: In test_start_logs_the_settings_and_runs_uvicorn, also capture `app` and assert it is the Starlette/ASGI app (not None, e.g. isinstance of the create_app return type), ran["host"] == settings host (set ENTERICH_HOST to a non-default value such as 127.0.0.2 so the assertion means something), ran["log_config"] is None and ran["access_log"] is False.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the gap. In src/enterich/__main__.py:37-45, main() calls uvicorn.run(create_app(settings), host=settings.host, port=..., log_config=None, access_log=False, proxy_headers=False, server_header=False). The only test that captures this call is tests/unit/test_main.py::test_start_logs_the_settings_and_runs_uvicorn. Its stub throws the app away (`lambda app, **kw: ran.update(kw)`) and it asserts only port, proxy_headers and server_header. test_start_carries_the_warnings stubs run without asserting anything. I searched all of tests/ (unit, integration, e2e, repo) and found nothing else that calls main() or checks log_config, access_log or host. The e2e and integration tests build the app in process through tests/integration/mcp.client, not through main(). The Dockerfile test stage only runs pytest on tests/unit and tests/integration, and CI does not start the container to check its logs.

The mutants are not equivalent:
- **log_config:** in uvicorn's Config.configure_logging, dictConfig runs whenever log_config is not None. Without log_config=None, uvicorn's default LOGGING_CONFIG adds its own non-JSON stderr handlers with propagate False. That breaks REQ-002-PRS-NF008 ("one JSON object per line, including lines from the libraries and the HTTP server", to stdout).

- **app:** passing None as the app breaks start-up.

So True or None makes uvicorn write access lines. These would still be JSON `library` lines, so this mutant is a weaker case against the spec than the others. Still, access_log=False is the code's intended behaviour, and asserting it fits the current specs.

I wrote a throwaway test at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/d9db8038-f808-4037-848d-89f7c08e07dd/scratchpad/t/test_probe.py. It sets ENTERICH_HOST=127.0.0.2, captures app as well, and asserts the app is non-None and callable, host == "127.0.0.2", log_config is None and access_log is False. claim: A return row's stock_qty is meant to be the taken quantity times the row's conversion_factor, but every test row has conversion_factor 1.0, so dividing, ignoring the factor, or reading the wrong key all pass.

REQ-005-PRS-F008's DoD asserts stock_qty −1 only for a factor of 1.
proposal: Add a row in a non-stock UOM (for example uom Box, conversion_factor 12, stock_qty 24 for qty 2), return 1 of it, and assert the row sent has qty −1 and stock_qty −12. Add a second case: a row whose conversion_factor is missing sends stock_qty equal to qty (kills _18).

verdict.reason: The gap is real. src/enterich/tools/returns.py:110 computes `line["stock_qty"] = -take * decimal(row.get("conversion_factor") or 1)`, and both sales and purchase returns use this `_line` (lines 143 and 169). Every test row comes from tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py:33-44 `row()`, which hard-codes uom "Nos", conversion_factor 1.0 and stock_qty == qty. The only stock_qty assertions (lines 151, 588 and 597-600) therefore compare stock_qty with qty at a factor of 1. A grep of all of tests/ (e2e included) for stock_qty, conversion_factor and uom turns up no other UOM. The e2e seed uses only stock_uom "Nos" and no e2e test makes a return. `mutmut show` confirms the diffs: _11 changes * to /, _14 changes `or 1` to `and 1`, _15/_16/_17 read a wrong key and fall back to 1, and _18 changes `or 2`. All six are listed in harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/survivors.jsonl. None is equivalent: with conversion_factor 12, _11 gives −1/12, _14-_17 give −1 and the original gives −12. _18 differs only on a row that has stock_qty but no conversion_factor or a zero one. That is unlikely in ERPNext, where conversion_factor is mandatory, but a cheap test still covers it. The behaviour can be seen in the request body sent to ERPNext. It is within the current spec: REQ-005-PRS-F008 builds the rows "from ERPNext's return of the invoice", which ERPNext computes as qty × conversion_factor, and its DoD asserts stock_qty −1. The fake already scales by conversion_factor (tests/fakes/erpnext.py:600-601). So an integration test is enough to close it: a row in Box with conversion_factor 12 and stock_qty 24 for qty 2, returned at 1, should be sent as qty −1 and stock_qty −12. It needs no spec, ADR or code change.

claim: Nothing checks that a start without warnings logs the `start` line at info level: forcing WARNING always passes, so every clean start would look like a warning.
evidence: Mutant enterich.__main__.x_main__mutmut_50 (`if (settings.warnings) or True`). test_start_carries_the_warnings asserts level 'warning' with warnings; test_start_logs_the_settings_and_runs_uvicorn never asserts the level.
proposal: In test_start_logs_the_settings_and_runs_uvicorn (ENV gives no warnings), assert line["level"] == "info" and line["warnings"] == [].

verdict.reason: I couldn't refute this finding; it holds. In src/enterich/__main__.py:25-26 the `start` line gets `logging.WARNING if settings.warnings else logging.INFO`. `mutmut show enterich.__main__.x_main__mutmut_50` reports the mutant as survived; it changes the condition to `(settings.warnings) or True`. The mutant is not equivalent, because the `level` field of the JSON line changes on every start without warnings. In tests/unit/test_main.py, only test_start_carries_the_warnings (line 59) checks the start line's level, and only for 'warning'. test_start_logs_the_settings_and_runs_uvicorn (lines 30-46) checks event, subject, leeway, that the secret is absent, and the uvicorn kwargs, but never the level or the warnings. The only other level assertion is tests/unit/test_log.py:25, which tests log.event directly and not main. tests/integration and tests/e2e have no start-level assertion. The behaviour is required: REQ-002-PRS-NF005 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:163, 171) says the http ERPNext URL and an unknown ENTERICH_ variable each "SHALL log a warning at start". So a clean start must not log a warning, and the REQ-002-PRS-NF008 table (line 209) gives every line a `level` field. I wrote a throwaway test in the scratchpad that runs main with ENV and asserts level == 'info' and warnings == []. It passes on the real code and fails on a mutated copy of src ("assert 'warning' == 'info'"). The fix is the proposed two assertions in test_start_logs_the_settings_and_runs_uvicorn, a test-only change within the current specs.

claim: The refusal of a return against a return is meant to name the invoice that the return is against, so the agent can retry with it; no test checks that this name appears, so dropping or misreading return_against passes.
evidence: Mutants enterich.tools.returns.x_invoice_of__mutmut_38 (against = None), _39, _40 and _41 (wrong key), _44 (the condition is always false). test_return_drafts.py::test_only_a_submitted_invoice_of_the_company_takes_a_return (case ACC-SINV-2026-00002, which is against INVOICE) and the purchase case at line 758 (against ACC-PINV-2026-00002) assert only 'a return' and the given name; test_a_return_without_its_invoice_is_refused_without_naming_none covers only the case with no return_against. (_46, the full stop changed, is noise.)
proposal: For the return-of-a-return cases, assert the refusal text contains the original invoice's name, for example f"({INVOICE})" for ACC-SINV-2026-00002, and the same on the purchase side.

verdict.reason: The finding holds. In src/enterich/tools/returns.py:76-81, invoice_of refuses a return of an invoice that is itself a return with "return_against: {name} is a return itself; give the invoice it returns (" + return_against + ")." and drops the parenthesis when return_against is empty. I printed the diffs with mutmut show. Mutants _38 (against = None), _39 (doc.get(None)), _41 (doc.get("RETURN_AGAINST")) and _44 (condition `and False`) each remove the "(ACC-SINV-2026-00001)" part from the refusal text, so they are not equivalent. The refusal text is all that changes, and the agent can see it. _46 only changes the full stop (".") to "XX.XX", which is noise as the finding says. No test checks that the original invoice's name appears. In tests/integration/test_return_drafts.py, the case at line 254 (ACC-SINV-2026-00002, a return against INVOICE = ACC-SINV-2026-00001) asserts only the given name and "a return". The purchase case at line 758 (return_against ACC-PINV-2026-00002) does the same. test_a_return_without_its_invoice_is_refused_without_naming_none (line 737) covers only the case with no return_against. Searches of tests/e2e and the rest of tests/ for "return itself" or the original invoice's name in this refusal found nothing. I ran a throwaway probe: create_draft_sales_return against ACC-SINV-2026-00002 returns "...give the invoice it returns (ACC-SINV-2026-00001).", and asserting f"({INVOICE})." in the text passes on the current code. Every non-noise mutant would fail that assertion. The probe ran from a temporary copy in tests/integration that I deleted right after; git status shows only the run directory that was already there. The REQ-004-PRS-F007 and REQ-005-PRS-F008 texts say only that such a return is refused, without naming the original. But REQ-001-P4-2 and URS-F006 ask for refusals that say what to change, and the code deliberately names the original (the no-None test exists for that path). A test that pins this behaviour stays within the current specs. Fix: in both return-of-a-return cases, sales and purchase, assert that the refusal text contains the original invoice's name in parentheses.
